title: HarborGrid - fallout contained and hardenings playbook transfer
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-11-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Almeida (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marco Li (Redwood CSM), Evan Park (HarborGrid SRE), Nora Vasquez (HarborGrid Platform), Samir Iqbal (HarborGrid CISO), Lena Ortiz (HarborGrid PO)
summary: Brief post-incident wrap; confirmed containment, reviewed root cause (KV cache eviction + prefix collision under burst), agreed immediate hotfix timeline, long-term hardenings and runbook transfer, compliance note from security. Actionable handoff to HarborGrid ops and Redwood SE for pilot of hardened cache and chaos testing.
topics: Root cause analysis (KV cache eviction + prefix collision)
Short-term mitigation: knob changes, canary patch
Long-term hardenings: checksums, deterministic eviction, telemetry
action_items: Priya Rao - ship canary hotfix to staging and run 24h smoke (due 2026-11-16)
Evan Park - provide exploded logs and sample request traces from 2026-11-08 incident (due 2026-11-15)
Marco Li - update runbook doc and share link to HarborGrid (due 2026-11-18)
Jordan Almeida - share cost estimate for dedicated cache nodes and pilot plan (due 2026-11-17)
next_steps: Priya to push canary and alert Redwood+HarborGrid on regression
Redwood SE to run benchmark with deterministic eviction enabled and share throughput/latency sheet

transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining uh we wanted to keep this tight, i know it's a busy week. we're here to close out the fallout from last monday's degradation and hand over the hardenings playbook.
[00:12] Evan (SRE): thanks Jordan, short version — incident contained, traffic restored after rollback, but we saw intermittent token timeouts and a growth in tail latency.
[00:24] Priya (SE): yeah right — root-cause appears to be the prefix cache eviction interplay with a recent routing change, two things happened: prefix collision increased and the eviction heuristic kicked in aggressively under burst, which caused KV cache churn. that churn created extra backend load and evicted some hot entries so latency spiked.
[00:43] Nora (Platform): just to be clear — are we saying the cache algorithm misidentified hot prefixes because of a routing policy change?
[00:50] Priya (SE): exactly, there was also a subtle bug where our prefix hash wasn't salted per-tenant so collisions were more likely when a burst of multi-tenant traffic occurred — that made a local hot key look cold elsewhere.
[01:05] Samir (CISO): from security perspective we need the audit trail for any data that was inspected during the failover, and also confirmation that no PII was retained in ephemeral logs.
[01:12] Marco (CSM): noted, we'll attach the audit logs and a short privacy note.
[01:18] Jordan (AE): okay, quick timeline review — incident started ~09:12 UTC, impact peaked at 09:23, mitigation (rollback) executed 09:42, full restoration 10:05. containment via rollback; we did not flip to dedicated capacity.
[01:36] Evan (SRE): correct. We also ran a limited canary post-restore and saw a small residual tail at 99.9 — probably from lingering KV misses.
[01:46] Priya (SE): actionables: immediate — we propose a canary hotfix that adds a per-tenant salt to prefix hashing and a defensive checksum on KV writes; medium term — deterministic eviction policy and stronger telemetry for prefix collision metrics; long term — evaluate dedicated cache nodes for high-tenancy customers.
[02:06] Lena (PO): what do you mean by deterministic eviction?
[02:10] Priya (SE): essentially move from an approximate LRU with probabilistic decay to a bounded, priority-driven eviction where we can pin hot prefixes for critical tenants and guarantee no cross-tenant churn. it's slightly more memory heavy but trades cost for predictable latency.
[02:28] Nora (Platform): cost is the main constraint — we need numbers: what is the expected cost delta if we pin X nodes for our tenant pattern?
[02:36] Jordan (AE): we'll produce a cost estimate; initial back-of-envelope suggests 12-18% infra delta for pinned caching vs current shared pool under your peak. we'll formalize.
[02:48] Samir (CISO): also SSO and KMS questions — during the incident we saw more auth latencies because of amplified token validation calls; how does the cache patch affect auth flows?
[02:58] Priya (SE): good call — the cache patch is only for model prefix keys, not auth tokens. we will ensure token caches remain unchanged; we'll add a safeguard that expiring token calls never trigger eviction heuristics for model keys.
[03:13] Evan (SRE): can we get the checklist for rollback and who hits which button? we want the ops playbook so we can run a drill.
[03:19] Marco (CSM): yes we'll hand over the runbook and schedule a transfer session.
[03:24] Jordan (AE): okay action items — Priya will push a canary patch to staging today, run 24h smoke, then to canary in prod limited to HarborGrid traffic; Evan will provide full trace dumps from the incident window; Marco will update the runbook doc; Jordan will share cost/dedicated node plan.
[03:40] Evan (SRE): small note — logs have some garbled hostnames from the time of the failover, looks like a log-rotation overlap. we'll surface the exact lines.
[03:48] Priya (SE): that's probably why some of the auto RCA tooling flagged odd latencies — transcription of host names caused grouping issues. we'll filter that.
[03:55] Samir (CISO): compliance checklist — SOC2 evidence, audit logs, data retention notes. i need documented confirmation that ephemeral logs with request payloads were not retained beyond 48h.
[04:06] Marco (CSM): we'll attach the retention export and a note; Priya can confirm how the hotfix treats ephemeral buffers.
[04:12] Priya (SE): confirmed — ephemeral buffers are in-memory and not persisted; we'll add a verification test to the canary.
[04:20] Lena (PO): on the product side, our success metric for this pilot is 99.95 P50 and P95 latency reduction for the heavy tail workloads and no more cross-tenant evictions.
[04:31] Jordan (AE): great, we'll aim for that in the benchmark.
[04:35] Priya (SE): also proposing a joint chaos run — synthetic multi-tenant bursts to validate eviction determinism and observe telemetry; tentative date 2026-11-30.
[04:46] Evan (SRE): that works for us.
[04:49] Jordan (AE): any blockers?
[04:51] Nora (Platform): only that we need the runbook in time to run internal drills before chaos day.
[04:57] Marco (CSM): we'll prioritize the runbook update.
[05:00] Jordan (AE): wrap up — recap of next steps and owners (see action items). we'll reconvene in one week to review staging canary results. thanks everyone.
[05:10] (end)
